source: EIA, US natural gas exports and re-exports by point of exit, 2022 annual: pipeline price 6.34 USD per thousand cubic feet (x 35.3147 Mcf per thousand m3); pipeline 3,040,787 and LNG 3,865,643 MMcf. LNG price: the US reference value (BACI 79,130 USD m, David 2026-10-24) less the pipeline value at the EIA price, over the EIA LNG volume
decided_by: Claude (beta v4 fixes thread; S16 energy-shock rerun 2026-10-26 18:26 UTC: LNG must not go below the BACI value)
basis: USA gas tonnes in BACI are estimated, so every route took the blended 405 USD m/bcm (USA-MEX pipeline 23.9 bn against 12.2 in BACI). P25 prices pipeline routes at the EIA pipeline price. The LNG routes first took the EIA LNG price (12.24 USD/Mcf, 432.3), which cut US gas exports to 64.8 bn against the 79.1 bn reference value David chose (BACI value over EIA volume); EIA's DOE-reported LNG prices sit below the customs values. The LNG price is now the residual that keeps the US total at that reference: (79,130 - 223.9 x 86.11 bcm) / 109.46 bcm = 546.8 USD m/bcm (15.5 USD/Mcf; BACI LNG value about 59.5 bn over EIA LNG volume gives 543). Extends the D-02 route pricing; GTAP 12 §12.3.6 sets one COMTRADE unit value per exporter.
